clue.text: A short jacket is dazzling

indicators.note: short means the word for the jacket loses its final letter

parts.note: a blazer is a kind of jacket

explanation.surface: Someone admires a brief, eye-catching jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts the last letter off BLAZER to give BLAZE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ablaze is burning brightly, hence dazzling to look at.

clue.text: Cave animal

parts.note: cave is Latin for 'beware', as on the old Roman doormat sign warning of a dog; here a farm sign warns walkers about a dangerous beast in the field

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cave' looks like a hollow in a rock, but it is the Latin imperative 'beware', pronounced as two syllables.
explanation.definitionFit: A field warning sign translated from Latin cave, telling walkers that a dangerous male bovine is about.

clue.text: A gallery under refurbishment could be that simple

definitions.text: A gallery under refurbishment could be that
definitions.meaning: a gallery closed for building works has had its pictures taken down, so it is without art

explanation.surface: A gallery being done up could end up looking plain and unsophisticated.
explanation.definitionFit: Artless means natural and unsophisticated, the plain sense of simple; read as two words it means lacking art.

clue.text: Drug to relieve asthma and hinder pee flowing!

indicators.note: flowing suggests the letters running freely into a new order

explanation.surface: A drug that helps breathing but also makes it hard to urinate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowing' rearranges HINDER PEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephedrine is a stimulant long used as a bronchodilator to ease asthma attacks.

clue.text: They're supposed to keep you quiet — situation with half the managers

definitions.text: They're supposed to keep you quiet

parts.note: a situation is a place or position

indicators.note: half the means only the first half of the word for managers is kept

parts.note: managers are bosses

explanation.surface: Something calming is found in a position alongside half of the management team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half the' keeps BOS, the first half of BOSSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Placebos are dummy pills given to pacify or humour a patient rather than to cure.

clue.text: I paced around Beijing initially — before discovering this?

definitions.text: I paced around Beijing initially — before discovering this?

indicators.note: around signals the letters being moved about
initially picks out the first letter of the city's name

explanation.surface: A visitor walked about Beijing before finding a ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges I PACED to PEDICA, and 'initially' gives B from Beijing; the whole clue pictures a tourist on foot before discovering a cycle rickshaw.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedicab is a pedal-powered rickshaw, common in Chinese cities, the transport a weary walker might find.

clue.text: Almost everything of poor quality in book

indicators.note: almost means the word is left one letter short of complete

parts.note: everything is all
bum is slang for worthless or of poor quality

explanation.surface: Nearly all of something shoddy is found in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims ALL to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: An album is a book of blank pages for stamps, photos or autographs.

clue.text: Top lady searched in the House of Lords?

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, the top lady
mined means dug or delved, searched for ore

explanation.surface: The Queen had a hunt around Parliament's upper chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: Peers wear robes trimmed with ermine at state occasions, so a peer in the House of Lords is ermined.
explanation.definitionFit: Ermined means wearing ermine fur, the robe trim of peers seated in the upper house.

clue.text: A town memento now recollected in song

indicators.note: recollected read as re-collected means the letters are gathered up again in a new order

explanation.surface: A souvenir of a town now remembered in a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' rearranges A TOWN MEMENTO NOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional English counting song about a man going out to cut a meadow with his dog.

clue.text: Boy interrupted by horrible woman was nervous

indicators.note: interrupted by means the boy's name is broken open by the other piece

parts.note: Ted is a boy's name
witch is an insult for a horrible woman

explanation.surface: A lad cut short by a nasty woman felt jittery.
explanation.definitionFit: Twitched means jerked or fidgeted, as one does when nervous.

clue.text: Dessert recipe in jacket

parts.note: a bombe is a frozen dome-shaped dessert
R is an abbreviation for recipe (Latin recipe, 'take')

explanation.surface: A pudding recipe found in a jacket pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'R' for recipe is the old prescription mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomber is a short waist-length jacket of the kind once worn by aircrew.

clue.text: Tongue supplied by butcher's emporium

indicators.note: supplied by means the letters are provided by the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Ox tongue bought from the butcher's shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supplied by' finds the letters across butchER'S Emporium.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is the Gaelic language of Scotland or Ireland, a tongue in the sense of language.

clue.text: Like written material, arranged in column with date

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Text set out in a column alongside a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges COLUMN with DATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Documental is an adjective meaning relating to or consisting of documents, written records.

clue.text: An elitist backing one form of "potty" art

indicators.note: backing means the words for an elitist are read in reverse

parts.note: a snob is an elitist
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A snobbish person supports one style of art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns A SNOB into BONSA. 'Potty' is a pun: the art is grown in a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonsai is the Japanese art of growing miniature trees in pots, so it is literally potted art.

clue.text: Advance with challenge that's personal

parts.note: to beard someone is to confront or challenge them boldly
own means belonging personally to someone

explanation.surface: Going forward with a dare that is individual.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear down is to move in on or approach in a threatening way, to advance on.

clue.text: A type of tree covered in fruit? It's only on the surface

indicators.note: covered in means one piece is wrapped inside the other

parts.note: a date is a fruit
the sorb is the service tree

explanation.surface: A tree that grows wrapped up in fruit, only on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a tree wrapped in fruit; 'covered in' is the container signal, and the sorb, or service tree, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: An adsorbate is a substance held as a thin layer on the surface of a solid, not absorbed into it.

clue.text: Stop trade, we say, in material for biological research

parts.note: to stem is to stop a flow

indicators.note: we say means the following word is heard as it is spoken

parts.note: to sell is to trade

explanation.surface: A ban on commerce in lab specimens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we say' turns SELL into its sound-alike CELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Stem cells are undifferentiated cells studied in biology and medicine for their capacity to become other cell types.

clue.text: Pasquale's receiving gift, the ultimate in fine wine

indicators.note: receiving means the setter's word takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: Pasquale is the setter, so his possession is my
alms are a charitable gift

indicators.note: the ultimate in means the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: The setter is given a present of the finest wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by their pseudonym, so the setter's name with 's gives the first-person possessive; 'receiving' and 'the ultimate in' are the signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Malmsey is a sweet fortified Madeira wine.

clue.text: Left good silver in enormous lidless cases, perhaps

indicators.note: in means the next pieces go inside the trimmed word
lidless in a down clue means the top letter is removed

parts.note: huge means enormous
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Silverware stored in huge open trunks.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the 'lid' is the top letter, so 'lidless' leaves UGE; 'in' then places the good silver inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Suitcases are an example of luggage, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Strength of character around university at a minimum — it's weak

indicators.note: around means the first piece goes round the next

parts.note: spine means backbone, courage or strength of character
U is the shortest form for university

explanation.surface: Someone's resolve barely touches the university, so it is feeble.
explanation.definitionFit: Supine figuratively means passive and spineless, failing to act: weak in will.

clue.text: Spotted animal (not lion) round capital of Chad, he being thirsty

indicators.note: round means the trimmed animal goes around the pieces after it
not means the lion's word is taken away

parts.note: a leopard is a spotted animal
Leo is the lion, the zodiac sign

indicators.note: capital of means the first letter of the place name

explanation.surface: A leopard roams through Chad, parched with thirst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes the lion to leave PARD, an old word for a leopard; 'capital of' gives the C and 'round' wraps the animal about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Parched means dried out, so a parched person is very thirsty.

clue.text: Jewellery clutched by lovely lady coming against king — someone in the tower?

indicators.note: coming against means the next piece is placed up against the first
clutched by means the jewellery is held inside the lady

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman
a ring is a piece of jewellery
R is Rex, king

explanation.surface: A beauty grasps her jewels as she meets the king; who is locked in the tower?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a prisoner in the Tower of London, but it is a church bell tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell-ringer pulls the ropes in a church belfry, which is a tower.

clue.text: One Indian female high up in another Asian land

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a rani is an Indian queen or princess, a woman of high rank

explanation.surface: An Indian noblewoman is found living abroad in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' contrasts with India: the land is Iran.
explanation.definitionFit: Irani is an adjective meaning of or from Iran, a different Asian country from India.

clue.text: Ceremony appropriate for audience

indicators.note: for audience means the word is as heard by listeners

parts.note: right means proper or appropriate

explanation.surface: A ceremony fit for spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for audience' turns RIGHT into the sound-alike RITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a formal religious or solemn ceremony.

clue.text: Country airs composed about America

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the next piece
composed means the letters are put together in a new order

parts.note: US is the United States, America

explanation.surface: A nation's tunes written about the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'airs' looks like tunes or pretensions; 'composed' rearranges it into RSIA, and 'about' puts that round the abbreviation for America.
explanation.definitionFit: Russia is a country spanning Europe and Asia.

clue.text: Religious song beginning again, containing a denunciation

indicators.note: containing means the pieces before hold the next one inside

parts.note: an anthem is a choral piece sung in church

indicators.note: beginning means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A hymn starting over includes a formal curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning' takes A from 'again'; 'containing' then puts A inside ANTHEM+A.
explanation.definitionFit: Anathema is a formal ecclesiastical curse, a solemn denunciation.

clue.text: Put tiny boy in gym in school break?

indicators.note: in means the first pieces go inside the word for gym

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym
lay means put or place
Tim, from Tiny Tim, the small boy in Dickens's A Christmas Carol

explanation.surface: Placing a small lad in a gym lesson during recess.
explanation.walkthrough: PE (physical education) is the school gym lesson; 'in' signals that the put and the tiny boy go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Playtime is the break between lessons when schoolchildren play outdoors.

clue.text: Bequeaths money to old women's society after death

indicators.note: after means the remaining pieces follow the word for death

parts.note: end means death, the end of life
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A will leaves money to an old ladies' club after someone dies.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to give a permanent fund or income, especially by will, to an institution.
